rationale:
Mara Voss as a trench surgeon, not a paramedic: grimy canvas greatcoat, rubber apron, welding goggles over a steel respirator, and an oversized powered bone-saw hanging from her fist. 22 colours in four material families — dirty olive canvas (c/e/v), near-black leather and rubber (b/B), scuffed steel (m/M/n), rust livery (l/L/i) — anchored on plum-black #120b10 as the continuous silhouette ink. No magenta, no chartreuse. A deterministic 7-10% speckle pass on the canvas, rubber and trousers supplies the fine-pixel grit the direction asks for without dissolving into noise; blood stains (x) are hand-placed on the apron, chest plate and boot toes. Proportions are 18px head over a 61px figure — 3.4 heads — with fists nearly half a head wide and the saw running a third of the body height.

Structurally the sprite is built for a top-down dimetric camera. The head sits on three rows of bare, lit skin only 8px wide between a 22px hood and a 28px shoulder line, so there is a real notch in silhouette and a warm mid-value band in grayscale. Arm inner edges are held 2px clear of the torso from row 30 down so the limbs stay separate limbs after downscaling. Nothing rises above the shoulder line — deliberately no pack, no shoulder-slung weapon, no antenna.

What it sacrifices: the pose is a planted idle, symmetric apart from the saw and a rust unit-stripe on her left shoulder cap, so it has no motion energy — this is a base frame, not an action beat. The palette is deliberately narrow-value and drab, so the sprite carries less colour appeal than a brighter treatment would; the rust cross and the amber power cell are the only saturated notes, and they are budgeted to roughly 5% of pixels. The dense grit also means this design is expensive to re-author across facings and animation frames by hand — it wants the speckle to be generated, not hand-placed.
frontFacingCue: A three-band face plane, each band separating hard in value from the one above it. The hood shell is mid canvas; inside it a continuous ink rim (row 7) opens onto a goggle band whose glass runs #dde3da/#8fa39c — the brightest cluster anywhere on the sprite — split by a dark #3c3936 nose bridge into two symmetric lenses. Below that, a steel respirator with a bright #bab4a7 vent grille sits between two visible skin cheeks, and a lit #b47c57 jaw and neck drop out under it. Symmetric hardware reinforces it: paired hose ports on both cheeks, paired lens glints, a paired strap line. The rejected sprite failed because its hood, hair and head were all one value with no interior plane; here the head reads as a lit surface pointed at the camera, and the bright goggle bar plus warm jaw are the two things that survive furthest down the size ladder.
smallCheck:
Survives, with real losses — I rendered it at 28px tall and inspected it magnified. What holds: the head still reads as a head facing you, because the pale goggle bar collapses into a single bright horizontal dash across a dark helmet mass and the warm jaw/neck pixels stay distinct from the black collar. The neck notch survives, so the head does not weld to the shoulders. The saw reads as a pale wedge hanging at her left, which keeps the silhouette asymmetric and armed. The boot flare and the crotch gap survive because I pushed the inner leg edges to pure ink specifically for this.

What is lost: the rust cross degrades from a clean cross into an orange smear — legible as "there is a marking on the chest", not as "medic". I widened the bars and pushed the lit half to #c87a52 to buy that much; a genuine cross at 28px would need the plate to be roughly twice its current size, which would unbalance the 48px master. The grit pass, the knuckle plates, the belt pouches, the hoses and the shoulder stripe all disappear into texture. The arms merge visually with the torso in the upper third despite the 2px gutters.

Honest verdict: if 28px is the shipping size, this design still works as a silhouette-and-face read, but the medic identity would need to move from the chest cross to something coarser — a full rust shoulder or a rust-coloured hood — and the grit pass becomes wasted budget.
